top_choice_rationale: P001 (Balasubramanian and Klenerman) recognises a defined chemical invention, reversible-terminator fluorescent nucleotides on clonally amplified single-molecule clusters, that turned a polymerase reaction into a parallel digital readout. It is mature after two decades of independent confirmation, has changed what researchers and clinicians can do, and the two-name allocation avoids a priority dispute over Mayer, Ju and Rothberg that the record cannot settle. The citation states the chemical basis. P002 (Buchwald and Hartwig) has the cleanest attribution and a real ligand-design problem, but it reads as an extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize and serves a narrower constituency, so it ranks second; an award is still preferable to none.
